answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful, time-delayed stake — a kernel of value that is slashed if the identity misbehaves. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn that stake back through useful work. Like jade, the stake is scarce and hard to fake cheaply; like a meadow that only grows where tended, reputation accrues slowly, so a fresh fake has no history to spend. Attackers face a real, upfront cost per identity, not just a free copy.
